purpose: Replace mistaken dolphin identity with existing gray shark; rebuild original mouth anatomy.

arguments.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Redraw Image 1, the exact original SLEVEJM2 005 sprite, as one polished cartoon SHARK sprite. Image 1 controls pose, mouth shape, facing, visible anatomy, framing and water occlusion. Images 2 and 3 are CHARACTER DESIGN AND DRAWING STYLE ONLY, not pose. Match the established shark: neutral medium gray skin, pale ivory jaw and underside, gill slits, bold black outlines, smooth restrained cel shading, heavy sly brows and razor-sharp triangular teeth. This is the sneaky shark character, never a friendly dolphin; no dolphin beak or rounded dolphin teeth. Pose: Right-facing upright shark in rear three-quarter view, head slightly bowed and thick rounded back. The eye sits high in the compact upper head. An open toothy mouth is visible directly below the short upper snout. The lower jaw projects horizontally toward the right with a distinctly drooping rounded end; this is cartoon SHARK JAW anatomy, not a long dolphin beak. Gray back/flank dominates; pale belly is narrow at right. Near pectoral fin hangs down along the flank and dorsal fin extends back-left. Do not add a far front fin missing from source. Preserve the source silhouette and relative positions while replacing pixel steps with smooth ink. Only the character parts above water are drawn, with a thin cyan-and-white ripple at original cutoff. Do not complete submerged body, tail or legs. One character only. All contours inside canvas with clear transparent padding on every edge. Actual transparent RGBA background, no checkerboard, scene, cast shadow, glow, text or collage.
